question: The ligature mark in typical hanging is characterised by which combination of features?

answers.text: Horizontal, at or below the thyroid cartilage, continuous around the neck

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. These features describe ligature strangulation, not hanging. In strangulation, the rope/ligature is applied horizontally at or below the level of the thyroid cartilage by an external force.

answers.text: Oblique, above the thyroid cartilage, discontinuous (interrupted at the knot)

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The hanging mark is: OBLIQUE (angled upward toward the suspension point), ABOVE the thyroid cartilage (high on the neck), and DISCONTINUOUS — it is interrupted at the point of knot/suspension. These three features together distinguish hanging from strangulation.

answers.text: Oblique, below the thyroid cartilage, continuous around the neck

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. In hanging, the mark is above the thyroid cartilage (not below) and is discontinuous (not continuous). A continuous, low mark suggests strangulation.

answers.text: Horizontal, above the thyroid cartilage, discontinuous at the knot

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. In hanging, the mark is oblique (slanted upward), not horizontal. A horizontal mark at any level is more characteristic of strangulation.

overallFeedback.feedback: Hanging mark: OBLIQUE + ABOVE thyroid cartilage + DISCONTINUOUS (interrupted at knot). Strangulation mark: HORIZONTAL + AT/BELOW thyroid cartilage + CONTINUOUS. These differences are essential for medicolegal differentiation.
Correct. Hanging ligature mark: OBLIQUE + ABOVE thyroid cartilage + DISCONTINUOUS at knot. Commit this triad to memory.
